REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT BIVAHENO PINOY U PUAXAD, A. Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE JAN üoi24 DIR. PEDRO A NOVAL, JR. CESO 111 Regional Director DILG Region VIII Kanhuraw Hills, Tacloban City Dear Dir. Noval: DILG Legal Opinion No. 10 s. 2012 We write regarding your 28 November 2011 letter which refers to the Central Office, for a more authoritative opinion, the 23 November 2011 ISt Endorsement of DBM Region VIII Director Imelda C. Laceras which refers to the Department the 25 October 2011 request for opinion of Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PHIC) Region VIII Vice President Walter R. Bacareza on the propriety of charging the Philhealth premium contributions of the Non-NHTS indigents enrollees to the 20% Development Fund. Based on the letter of PHIC Regional Vice President Walter R. Bacareza, enrollees of indigents to the PHIC are classified in two (2) categories, namely: National Household Targeting System (NHTS), whose premium contributions are shouldered by the national government; and Non-NHTS, whose premium contributions are shouldered by the local government units. As opined in the 23 November 2011 ISt Endorsement of DBM Director Imelda C. Laceras, the "DBM takes the position that the said program may be allowed to be charged against the 20% Development Fund" based on the following grounds, to wit: "Under section 4.0 of DILG-DBM JMC No. 2011-1 (prohibited expenditure items) the payment of premium contribution of indigents under the Non-NHTS, is not among those PS items mentioned. What was mentioned are those administrative expenditures that are not related to and/or not connected with the implementation of development projects, programs and activities. " Before we address your query, it should be noted that during the July 2011 meeting of representatives of the Central Office with representatives of the DBM Central Office, it was discussed therein that the utilization of the 20% development fund is not limited to the enumerated environmental management, social and economic development projects under DILG-DBM JMC No. 2011-1. Hence, the pressing need for issuance of joint clarificatory guidelines on the implementation of DILG-DBM JMC No. 2011-1 to further illuminate on the scope as well as the prohibited expense items. To date however, said clarificatory guidelines are pending issuance. In view thereof, we shall issue an opinion on the query through an interpretation of DILG-DBM JMC No. 2011-1 as written, in relation to the pertinent provision of the 1991 Local Government Code (the "Code"). Upon reading of the opinion rendered by DBM Region VIII Director Laceras, this level is inclined to agree with her conclusion that indeed, Philhealth premium contributions of the Non-NHTS indigents enrollees may be charged against the 20% Development Fund. However, our conclusion is based on an entirely different ground. This level opines that the matter to be determined herein is whether the payment of PHIC premiums is a project covered by the 20% Development Fund utilization and NOT whether said project expense is covered by the prohibition.

It must be borne in mind that the enumerated prohibited expense items refers to those incidental expenses incurred in the implementation of development projects. In this case, payment of indigent PHIC premiums subsidized by the LGUs is mandated by law (RA 7875, as amended by RA 9241) and is not an incidental expense to the "project" but refers to the "project" itself, i.e., LGU sponsorship of PHIC premium contributions of indigents which falls under the LGUs' medical assistance/social health insurance financing program as devolved thereto by the national government. LGU sponsored PHIC premium contribution of indigents is a primary health care project of the national government and is one of the basic services devolved by law to the LGUs under Section 17 of the 1991 Local Government Code (the "Code"). Notably, Sections 16 and 17 of the Code offers strategic insights on the emphasis and content of local development. Hence, DILG-DBM JMC No. 2011-1 should be interpreted in conjunction therewith. Considering the above premises, we opine that Philhealth premium contribution of the Non-NHTS indigent enrollees is a development project (primary health care project) chargeable to the 20% Development Fund. We hope the foregoing sufficiently addresses your concern. Very truly yours, JESUS DO UE, IV Directo II LS.08
